width.description: world units = px of the terrain artwork; every position is in this space

bounded.description: the reader's camera stays on the terrain (`WorldMap.bounded`)

MapSettings.description: The document `map`: the world map's own settings

minZoom.description: shown only from / up to this zoom (e.g. a street-detail layer for the city)

tiles.description: the same layer as a tile pyramid for deep zoom (BACKLOG 10.63; `scripts/map-tiles.mjs` renders it from `image`): `{path}/{z}/{x}_{y}.webp`, `TILE_PX` square; level z draws 2^z px per world unit (0 … `levels`). The image stays the base (and the fallback while tiles load); the tiles on screen draw over it from level 1.

fog.description: fog of war (owner 2026-10-12: "am Anfang ist erstmal nichts drauf, und dann, wie ein Fog of War, gewinnt die Karte da, wo man war, in einem gewissen Umkreis an Farbe"): the reader draws this layer only within `radius` world units of the places the reader has unlocked (the save game's `map.places`), soft at the edge – over a plain layer of the same shapes (the plaster model). The builder shows it whole.

levels.description: the deepest level (2^levels px per world unit)

minLevel.description: the coarsest level with tiles (owner 2026-10-12: "like Google Maps / OpenStreetMap" – every level the same 256 px tiles, a coarse one covering more of the world): ≤ 0 = the whole pyramid is tiles, the layer's image is never loaded and the coarsest tiles on screen stand in while sharper ones load; missing = 1 (levels below 1 are the image)

px.description: a tile's edge in px: `TILE_PX` (256, the default) or 512 – four times fewer images per screen (owner 2026-10-12)

radius.description: world units around an unlocked place where the layer shows fully (it fades out over `FOG_FEATHER` × radius beyond)
